ArXiv cs.AI.title: More Rules, Longer Lists? Benchmarking Self-Evolving Agents on a Hidden-Rule Curriculum
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.40758v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Self-evolving agents rewrite a persistent state from feedback, but it is largely untested whether this lets them learn a rule nobody told them. An agent can also pass by writing down each correction as an exception, and its list then grows with every new rule. We introduce CLR-Bench, a Curriculum of Latent Rules benchmark. Each chain adds one hidden rule per level on top of the earlier ones. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Beyond Plausible Prediction: Safety Sufficiency in Web World Models
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.40798v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Web world models increasingly predict the consequences of candidate actions before agents act, yet a plausible predicted future does not necessarily support the correct safety decision. In a matched human evaluation of 3,000 predictions from ten frozen open models, 86.1% are judged semantically plausible. However, several models exhibit highly asymmetric authorisation behaviour, combining low false-safe execution with poor recall of clarifiable ASK cases and a strong preference for BLOCK. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Circumventing the Computational Hardness of Computational Arbitrage
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.40831v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI model marketplaces host providers with heterogeneous costs and capabilities. These differences create an opportunity for computational arbitrage (Olmedo et al., 2026), in which an intermediary purchases inference from a portfolio of models and resells it to users at a profit. Beyond creating profit opportunities for the arbitrageur, computational arbitrage offers financial value to both consumers and providers and could therefore significantly influence AI model markets. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Incongruence-Aware Evaluation of Multimodal Speech Emotion Recognition in Audio Large Language Models
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.40883v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Voice-interactive large language models process both what a speaker says and how they say it, yet the two channels do not always agree. We ask whether that disagreement degrades speech emotion recognition. Mapping text and audio into a shared valence-arousal-dominance space, we convert the distance between them into a continuous, threshold-free incongruence score with a two-component Gaussian mixture, and validate the score against human judgement. ArXiv cs.AI.title: ChatGPT as a Surveillance Assistant? An Exploratory Case Study of AI-Assisted Surveillance Risks
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.40890v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate detailed guidance, functional code, and persuasive text at scale. As one of the most widely used consumer language model products as of 2026, ChatGPT gives broad public access to these capabilities, motivating concerns about its potential use in surveillance-related tasks. We present an exploratory case study of what potentially harmful surveillance assistance looks like in ChatGPT's public web interface. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Does Recursive Knowledge Construction Help Agents Verify Consensus Claims in Science?
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.40906v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent scientific agents build knowledge recursively by retrieving evidence, constructing an intermediate state, and judging whether that state contains sufficient information. These agents are evaluated end-to-end, usually without ground truth, so the effect of each design choice is unknown. Here, we examined two design axes: (1) what the recursion builds (the state of evidence) and (2) what controls it (the judge that decides when to stop). ArXiv cs.AI.title: Towards Portable Specification of the Agent Harness
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.40917v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models act only through the infrastructure that surrounds them. That infrastructure, the harness, determines what a model can accomplish and how it fails, yet it has no settled definition. To address this gap, we decompose the harness into eight functional components that can be specified and compared across systems, and we propose a portable specification framework that records which model ran in which harness. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Agentic World Modeling for Agent Test-time Scaling without Environment Replica
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.40927v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Test-time scaling (TTS) improves large language model agents by sampling and selecting among multiple candidate trajectories, but common realizations assume that these trajectories can be executed in parallel. This assumption breaks in realistic deployments, where enterprise workspaces and cloud services are shared and persistent, costly or infeasible to replicate, and actions may introduce irreversible side effects or cross-trajectory interference. Existing generative world models avoid direct execution, but typically compress environment state

ArXiv cs.AI.title: DiRAFT: Privacy-Aware Financial Transcript Synthesis from Aggregate Discourse Priors
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.40938v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Using customer conversations to train and evaluate financial language models raises confidentiality concerns because non-public financial facts can remain after direct identifiers are masked. Synthetic transcripts offer an alternative data source, but their discourse fidelity and residual confidentiality risks require assessment. We introduce DiRAFT (Discourse Realization from Aggregate First-order Transitions), which extracts financial concept graphs and records the order in which concepts are first introduced. ArXiv cs.AI.title: The First Few Tokens Matter: Understanding Chain-of-Thought Controllability
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.40939v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is a promising way to oversee increasingly capable agents. It succeeds in part because current models appear limited in their ability to control what they verbalize in their reasoning traces. We investigate the source of this limitation and link it to an entropy collapse in the first few tokens following the opening thinking tag. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Benchmarking Forecasting Agents on Yesterday's Tomorrows
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.40940v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Digital agents can now gather and organize information, reason over it, and use tools to complete complex tasks. Forecasting puts all of these abilities to the test: it requires integrating incomplete evidence, inferring causal drivers, and committing to calibrated probabilistic judgments. Existing benchmarks are poorly suited to measuring and improving this ability. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Opening the Box Changes the Cat: LLMs Detect Chain-of-Thought Monitoring - What now?
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.40946v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning allows large language models (LLMs) to generate intermediate reasoning traces in natural language while solving complex tasks. These traces can support safety monitoring by exposing potentially harmful plans before actions are executed. In this work, we investigate the conditions under which LLMs infer the presence of CoT monitoring from direct and indirect environmental cues and examine how this inference affects their subsequent behavior. ArXiv cs.AI.title: P-ContextBench: From Personal Fact Recall to Personalized Agent Behavior
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.40959v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for personal tasks, yet evaluating their safe use of personal context remains difficult because such contexts are private, fragmented, dynamic, and socially situated. We introduce P-ContextBench, a realistic, verifiable, and scalable benchmark for evaluating personal-context understanding. P-ContextBench constructs population-structured, life-story-grounded digital humans from demographic seeds reflecting the U.S. population. ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.40970v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generative audio systems can produce large libraries of personalized bedtime content, but ordinary media objectives (retention, completion, and novelty) are poorly aligned with the goal of supporting a transition toward sleep. Direct evidence for narrated bedtime audio in adults is mixed, and a recent active-controlled trial did not support such audio as a standalone treatment for sleep disturbance. ArXiv cs.AI.title: The psychophysics of affect in large language models
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.40985v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Good decisions often require considering how outcomes will feel. Yet large language models (LLMs) increasingly enter decision workflows, despite little being known about how they map outcomes to feelings or use those mappings in choice. We tested how LLMs anticipated gambling or stock-trading outcomes would feel and whether they incorporated these ratings into choice. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Automatic Construction of Strong Simple Baselines
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.40700v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: To rigorously establish the value of a novel deep learning method, it must be compared against appropriate baselines. As deep learning has become increasingly common in the physical and life sciences, there have been numerous cases in which apparent progress has turned out to be an artifact of omitted or missing baselines. In this work, we investigate whether this problem can be mitigated by using large language models to automate the construction of baselines. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Bayesian Distribution System State Estimation with Flow Matching
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.40728v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Medium-voltage feeders have few real-time measurements, so distribution system state estimation (DSSE) rests on pseudo-measurements of the secondary substations, a prior in Bayesian terms. Weighted least squares keeps the power flow exact but reduces this prior to a mean and variance, while supervised deep learning estimators also learn the power flow and are tied to one measurement set. We propose PoSE (posterior sampling for state estimation), which keeps the Bayesian structure of DSSE and learns only what the distribution system operator does

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Don't Just Impute, Detect: Task-Aware Diffusion Pipelines for Edge Anomaly Detection
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.40732v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) edge pipelines routinely lose contiguous blocks of multi-sensor data to network dropouts and hardware faults. The standard remedy is a disjointed "impute-then-detect" pipeline whose imputer is trained only for Mean Squared Error (MSE). Such an imputer fills a missing block with the most probable normal pattern: a partially observed anomaly is smoothed back toward normality, and boundary artifacts on normal data raise false alarms. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Unsupervised Feature Selection Using Local Intrinsic Dimensionality -- Extended Version
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.40736v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: High dimensionality degrades both the efficiency and the effectiveness of learning algorithms, and in many applications no class labels are available to guide dimensionality reduction. This paper proposes LIDFS, an unsupervised feature selection method based on Local Intrinsic Dimensionality (LID). The method builds on the formal equivalence between LID and the indiscriminability of distance measures. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Certified Behavioral Retention for Continual Adaptation with Held-Out Anchors
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.40740v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Continual adaptation requires deciding not only how to update a model, but whether to commit an update without exceeding a declared budget for changes to protected behavior. We introduce Certified Anchor-Based Adaptation (CABA), a candidate-agnostic post-update gate that reserves historical observations from candidate optimization, compares old and candidate policies on frozen representations, and selects the largest tested interpolation coefficient whose worst-anchor forward KL divergence remains within budget. ArXiv cs.LG.title: AutoHebb: Self-Modifying Neural Networks that Zero-Shot Infer and Continually Learn
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.40757v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Humans and animals have a unique capacity to generalize and learn in novel circumstances, including "0-shot" inference (ZI) and continual learning (CL) -- two powerful cognitive abilities. Despite this importance, efforts to model ZI and CL are seriously limited in several ways. First, existing models typically lack components critical to ZI and CL in the brain, namely, strong inductive biases (for ZI) and autonomous control of learning (for CL). ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.40857v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Scientific foundation models (SciFMs) have achieved remarkable performance on a wide range of PDEs, including the ability to efficiently adapt to unseen data distributions with additional finetuning. As with all neural architectures, finetuning such models comes with the risk of catastrophic forgetting, whereby adapting to new tasks degrades prior knowledge of the model. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.40858v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Training a large language model is compute-bound, and current recipes divide the work between optimizers by hand: orthogonalized momentum for attention and MLP matrices, Adam-style updates for the rest. This division rests on human priors about which layer type deserves which geometry, and it fixes a single global update budget that every parameter block shares. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.40861v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study first-order regret guarantees for adversarial bandits with a fixed, known directed feedback graph. For strongly observable graphs, [ACBDK15] establishes a minimax regret of $\widetilde{\Theta}(\sqrt{\alpha T})$, where $\alpha$ denotes the independence number of the graph and $T$ denotes the horizon. ArXiv cs.LG.title: TensorSSM: Memorizing Spatial Position in Dynamic State Space for Tensor Core Generation
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.40871v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: High-dimensional tensors are ubiquitous in real-world applications but lead to massive storage overhead. Functional tensor decomposition addresses this by employing neural networks to map element coordinates to tensor cores, significantly reducing the parameters for data compression. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.40901v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As publications and products on time series forecasting (TSF) proliferate, researchers face a growing burden of analyzing existing work. First, not all publications release code. For instance, only about 20% of arXiv TSF papers have a code link in the surveyed period. Second, released code also requires manual maintenance. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.40914v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Training acceleration methods for diffusion transformers, such as REPA and dispersive regularization, are commonly explained by additional supervision, spatial-structure priors, or improved feature geometry. We revisit this view and uncover a striking internal change: the AdaLN-Zero residual gate $\alpha$, which directly controls how conditioned updates enter the residual stream, is substantially reorganized by these methods. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.40934v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this work, we provide a formal framework and mathematical definition for the subset of foundation models focused on enabling the property of "any-task inference" (ATI) (similar to zero-shot inference), rather than those designed for pre-training fine-tuning. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.40936v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recommendation systems that optimize for the average user can fail to capture the preferences of diverse demographic groups. We consider a dynamic recommendation system, where arriving users can belong to different demographic groups. Importantly, these groups can intersect, and a user may belong to several groups. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.40943v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The bottleneck of attention mechanisms, which are the fundamental building block of modern language models, is their quadratic complexity in terms of context size. There has thus been an increasing interest in the compression of the context, also called KV-cache compression.
